title: FERPA - student education records
facts: FERPA is a federal law protecting privacy of student education records at schools that receive funds under applicable U.S. Department of Education programs.

FERPA generally gives parents rights to inspect and review education records, seek amendment of inaccurate or misleading records, and control certain disclosures of personally identifiable information.
When a student turns 18 or attends a postsecondary institution, FERPA rights generally transfer from the parent to the eligible student.
FERPA contains exceptions allowing disclosure without consent in specified circumstances.
